thread_analysis.thread_summary: Alps Alpine (contact Hitomi Ohira, with engineering colleagues Masafumi Kaneko and Yuya Kitayama) works with Allion (sales contact Jun Wang, PM Toshitaka Mochizuki, with Itsuo Sakai and the AJ Bluetooth Group) on Bluetooth SIG certification for two automotive display/HMI models, HM23 and HM26. The thread (only 3 top-level messages, but with extensive nested quoted history spanning October through early December 2024) covers the full arc from quotation and registration-scope questions (DID purchase, End Product registration, Compliance Folder requirements, derivative-model test report reuse) through sample shipment and lab routing (Japan lab for RF full + RF PHY 1M mode, then Taiwan lab for remaining RF PHY modes, requiring export classification paperwork), to detailed RF/RF PHY test execution support: clarifying Test Plan/QRCT terminology, troubleshooting a blocked QDART/QRCT tool installation requiring potential Qualcomm vendor escalation, and verifying DUT/CSD/DC Power Supply wiring after a test sample stopped operating correctly.
all_questions_found: Is the newly purchased DID used for End Product registration rather than Controller subsystem DN reuse, and can RF/RF PHY test reports be reused for future Host-subsystem-only derivative models?
Does HM23 also need a quoted Compliance Folder creation and End Product registration scope, not just an additional RF test item?
Should manuals and design documents be submitted by email to the PM or via an SFTP server like the prior WiFi certification process, and can the test schedule be shared once confirmed?

What is a Test Plan, are the requested RF parameters QRCT settings, what tester equipment is being referenced, and what do the RF/RF PHY automated test procedure steps (Serial port/HCI connection, Baud Rate) actually require?
How can the QDART/QRCT tool installation error blocking DUT mode entry be resolved, and can Allion provide a working tool set or escalate to Qualcomm support?
Is the customer's DUT/CSD/DC Power Supply wiring correct, and what's the difference between the green and black cables on the CSD (CID/Meter) cable connector?

(Administrative, not a standalone case) Confirmation of three RF test parameters (Inband Image Frequency, Power Control, Enhanced Power Control) needed for Test Plan creation, ultimately obtained by the customer from Qualcomm.
(Operational, not a standalone case) Multiple rounds of meeting-time coordination between Alps Alpine and Allion staff to discuss open questions.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Registration scope logic distinguishes DN/test-report reuse (tied to whether the Controller subsystem changes) from DID purchase requirements (tied to each individual End Product registration, required regardless of reuse). RF test parameter values (Inband Image Frequency, Power Control, Enhanced Power Control) are Bluetooth SoC vendor-owned functionality, not QRCT tool settings, requiring confirmation from the SoC vendor (Qualcomm) rather than the test lab. Test execution required Allion's InterLab RF testsystem with Serial/Serial-over-USB-based automated command sequencing, and a customer-side QDART/QRCT installation failure (blocking DUT test-mode entry) was not resolvable from error/license information alone, leading to a recommended Qualcomm CASE support escalation alongside an interim workaround (lending a working PC or full tool set). A non-operating test sample also prompted a full DUT/CSD/DC Power Supply wiring cross-check against the vendor manual, surfacing an unresolved ambiguity about same-colored cables on the CSD (CID/Meter) connector.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Registration/test-reuse decisions track which physical subsystem (Controller vs. Host) actually changed, independent of administrative requirements like DID purchase that apply per registration. Test-environment tooling failures that can't be self-diagnosed by either party should be escalated to the SoC vendor's official support channel in parallel with a practical interim workaround, rather than left to indefinite internal troubleshooting.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Misapplying DID/DN reuse logic could cause a customer to skip a required per-registration DID purchase or unnecessarily repeat RF/RF PHY testing on an unchanged Controller subsystem. Treating SoC-vendor-owned parameters as test-tool settings could lead to an incorrectly scoped Test Plan. Leaving a tooling installation failure or wiring ambiguity unresolved could stall the entire RF/RF PHY test schedule.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: The written record does not show an explicit, unambiguous confirmation reply to the customer's DID/test-report-reuse question (case_01) or to the CSD cable color-difference question (case_06) within this thread — both appear to have been left for a verbal meeting discussion or remained genuinely unresolved in writing, which is worth flagging since email-only documentation trails should ideally capture the final answer even when discussed live.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For multi-model, multi-phase certification engagements (especially automotive HMI/display products spanning two model variants), keep registration-scope logic (DID purchase vs. DN/test-report reuse) and quote-scope logic (Compliance Folder/registration support vs. RF test item count) explicitly separated when answering customer questions, and ensure that any clarifications resolved verbally in meetings are still captured in a follow-up written confirmation to avoid an incomplete email record.
